key_insight: X-MuTeST integrates LLM-generated high-level semantic rationales with attention-enhancing training to improve both accuracy and explainability of hate speech detection across English, Hindi and Telugu.
problem_solved: Addresses low accuracy and poor interpretability of hate speech classifiers—especially for underexplored Indic languages—by providing a multilingual benchmark and a framework that leverages LLM reasoning to guide model explanations.
method: Build X-MuTeST: a multilingual human-annotated benchmark for hate speech (English, Hindi, Telugu) with explanation annotations.
Use LLMs to generate high-level semantic rationales (LLM-consulted explanations) for examples and incorporate these into supervision.
Combine rationale-guided loss with attention-enhancing techniques (e.g., attention regularization/explanation alignment) to train more interpretable classifiers.
impact: Provides practitioners a benchmark and a practical training recipe to produce more accurate, interpretable hate speech models for low-resource languages—improving trust, error analysis, and deployment readiness.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: data + LLM → extract rationales → attention-guided training → explainable classifier
Bar chart: performance (accuracy/F1) and explainability score comparisons across languages and baselines
Annotated example card: original post, LLM rationale, token-level attention heatmap, final prediction
Language map/icon set: dataset coverage and sample counts for English, Hindi, Telugu
paper_title: X-MuTeST: A Multilingual Benchmark for Explainable Hate Speech Detection and A Novel LLM-consulted Explanation Framework
paper_authors: Mohammad Zia Ur Rehman, Sai Kartheek Reddy Kasu, Shashivardhan Reddy Koppula, Sai Rithwik Reddy Chirra, Shwetank Shekhar Singh
